entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Crescens was a Galilean Christian missionary who appeared in the New Testament and is traditionally considered one of the 72 disciples sent out by Jesus in Luke 10. He is mentioned as a companion of Paul and played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in the region.

Crescens was born in the early 1st century CE and died around 100 CE. His name, 'Crescens', is the present-active participle of the Latin word crescere, meaning 'increasing'.

The significance of Crescens lies in his missionary work, which contributed to the growth of Christianity in the region. His relationship with Paul and the other apostles underscores the importance of his role in the early Christian community.

Crescens's legacy can be seen in the continued spread of Christianity in the region, which had a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization.

"In Galatia, where Crescens served as a missionary, he witnessed the early Christian community's dedication to their faith and their commitment to spreading the message of Jesus Christ."
